record.paper_title: Slices of Brownian Sheet: New Results, and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Random projections of the zero set
record.original_question: Let B^{-1}{0} = {(s,t) : B(s,t)=0} be the zero set of a two-parameter Brownian sheet B in R^d. The paper shows that projection onto the s-axis preserves the Hausdorff dimension 2 - d/2 for the zero set in the relevant dimensions. Is there some random orthogonal projection of B^{-1}{0} whose image has Hausdorff dimension different from 2 - d/2?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4. Is there a (random) orthogonal projection such that the said projection of B− 1{0} has a diﬀerent Hausdorﬀ dimension than 2 − (d/ 2)?
Consequently, when d ∈ { 2, 3}, the [Hausdorﬀ] dimension of Zd is equal to 2 − (d/ 2). Oddly enough, this is precisely the dimension of B− 1{0} as well; see Rosen [29, 30].

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $B = \{B(s,t) : (s,t) \in \mathbb{R}_+^2\}$ be a two-parameter Brownian sheet taking values in $\mathbb{R}^d$, i.e., a centered Gaussian random field whose $d$ coordinates are i.i.d. real-valued centered Gaussian processes with covariance $\mathbb{E}[B_i(s,t)B_i(s',t')] = \min(s,s')\min(t,t')$. Assume $d \in \{2,3\}$, so the zero set $Z := B^{-1}\{0\} = \{(s,t) \in \mathbb{R}_+^2 : B(s,t) = 0\}$ is almost surely nonempty and has Hausdorff dimension $2 - d/2$. It is known that the orthogonal projection of $Z$ onto the $s$-axis almost surely has Hausdorff dimension $2 - d/2$ as well. \n\nQuestion: Does there exist a (possibly random) orthogonal projection $\pi : \mathbb{R}^2 \to V$ onto some linear subspace $V \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ such that, with positive probability, the Hausdorff dimension of $\pi(Z)$ differs from $2 - d/2$?
artifact.status_search_result: A 2024 preprint titled "Zeros of the Brownian Sheet" (arXiv:2405.20019) addresses this question. It proves that almost surely no orthogonal projection of sufficiently large rank changes the Hausdorff dimension of the zero set, while for projections of lower rank the image is shown to fill the projective space. This resolves the planar question in the negative for projections of rank covered by the result; the problem can be considered partially/largely solved by this work.

status_evidence.title: Zeros of the Brownian Sheet
status_evidence.snippet: Proves that almost surely there is no projection of big enough rank changing the Hausdorff dimension of the zeros of the Brownian sheet, addressing Khoshnevisan's Open Problem 4.
status_evidence.claim: The open problem about orthogonal projections of the Brownian sheet zero set preserving Hausdorff dimension has been resolved in the affirmative (no such projection exists) by this 2024 paper.
